w: The Cadbury family built an entire village around their chocolate factory and banned pubs from it -- a Quaker experiment in a 'garden village' where alcohol was never sold. A century on, the Joseph Rowntree Foundation called it one of the nicest places to live in Britain.
s: A dry Quaker village built around a chocolate factory
_facts: 19th-century model village founded by the Quaker Cadbury family for factory employees
Designed as a 'garden'/'model' village where the sale of alcohol was forbidden
Home to the Cadbury's chocolate factory and the Bournville Centre for Visual Arts
A 2003 Joseph Rowntree Foundation study called it one of the nicest places to live in Britain
